subject: Renewal: 16→32 GPU capacity amendment — updated pricing and throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Rivas <sofia.rivas@horizonhealth.com>, procure@horizonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — current committed pool + expansion questions

Naomi,

We're starting our renewal conversations for our inference fleet that runs Horizon's triage and summarization pipelines. Current commitment is 16 reserved GPUs through July. Leadership is asking about an accelerated path to 32 reserved GPUs for Q3 — primarily to improve throughput during surge windows and to run heavier eval sweeps without affecting production latency.

Before we set a call: two asks from procurement and engineering 
- Can you share the latest per-hour reserved price for a straight 16→32 bump on a 12‑month term?
- What guarantees or SLOs can Redwood provide around sustained throughput and tail latency when we double the pool?

Our procurement team also needs a list of artifacts for the procurement package (SOC2 evidence, network diagram, revised quote).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Liam
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Horizon Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — current committed pool + expansion questions

Liam — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marcus (AE) for pricing and Evelyn (Sales Ops) for SLOs/procurement checklist.

Quick answers up front:
- We can offer an amended reserved-rate structure for a 12‑month addendum that effectively reduces the per-hour rate for the incremental 16 GPUs. I'll include a redlineable amendment.
- For throughput: Redwood will commit to a measured sustained throughput floor for the combined pool (16+16) during business hours plus a tail-latency SLO for 95th and 99th percentiles; specifics can be in the amendment.

Attaching: Redwood_Dedicated_32GPU_AMENDMENT_v3.pdf (draft pricing + SLA language) and a short procurement checklist.

If procurement wants it, we can produce a short mutual action plan with milestones — signature, ramp start, validation window, and canary rollback plan. Proposed time to ramp: 3 weeks after signature.

Would you be available Wednesday for a 30-minute call to walk the amendment?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_32GPU_AMENDMENT_v3.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), procurement_checklist.docx (stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — current committed pool + expansion questions

Hi Liam — following up with pricing specifics based on the attachment Naomi shared. Thank you for the context on the Q3 surges; that helps us tailor the economics.

Proposal highlights (12‑month term, effective on signature):
- Existing 16 GPUs: unchanged base rate.
- Incremental 16 GPUs (to reach 32): discounted per‑hour reserved rate of $1.12/hr per GPU (net of existing commitment) — this incorporates a volume rebate tied to the 12‑month commit.
- If Horizon issues an annual prepay, we can further reduce incremental rate to $0.98/hr per GPU.

Throughput & SLOs (included in amendment):
- Sustained throughput guarantee: baseline combined throughput >= 1.1M tokens/hour for standard gen workloads at 512 token context when autoscaling is active.
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 420ms, 99th <= 650ms for single-request small-batch traffic under normal operating conditions.
- Failure mode: if sustained throughput falls below guarantee for two consecutive 30‑minute windows, Redwood will (a) issue a credit equivalent to X% of hourly reserved charges during the outage window, and (b) accelerate capacity transiently from our burst pool while we remediate. Exact crediting math is in section 4 of the amendment.

Notes: the throughput guarantee assumes standard model selection (gpt-small-rlm equivalent) and no unthrottled batch jobs during the validation window — we'll define the validation harness in the MOP.

I've attached an updated pricing table in the amendment and flagged the sections that are usually negotiated.

— Marcus
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_32GPU_AMENDMENT_v3.pdf (pricing table, redlines)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Rivas <sofia.rivas@horizonhealth.com>, procure@horizonhealth.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — current committed pool + expansion questions

Thanks Marcus — that clarifies a lot. A couple of clarification items from engineering and procurement: 
1) The throughput number is helpful; can you confirm whether the 1.1M tokens/hour guarantee is per-cluster or per-tenant? Our usage is sharded across two logical tenants within our account.
2) For the failure-mode credits: procurement needs a simple formula and an example line-item for our budgeting. The amendment's legal phrasing is fine but we need a plain-English example.
3) We will likely take the 12‑month path, but we need the option to stop the incremental capacity after 6 months if usage doesn't justify the cost — is a 6-month opt-out on the incremental pool possible (with a 60-day notice)?

Also, our security team sent SCP questions; attaching Horizon_SCQ_Response_v2.xlsx with a few asks. We'd like SOC2 AOC and an updated network diagram in the procurement bundle.

If acceptable, can Redwood produce the example credit calculation and confirm opt-out mechanics by COB Friday?

— Liam
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonhealth.com>, procure@horizonhealth.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — current committed pool + expansion questions

Hi Liam — quick operational answers from the infra/ops side: 
- The 1.1M tokens/hour guarantee is scoped to your account's Dedicated pool (i.e., combined capacity post-amendment). If you maintain two logical tenants inside that pool, the guarantee applies to the pool aggregate. If you need tenant-level SLAs, we can scope that into the MOP but it requires separate metering.
- Credit example (plain English): suppose reserved incremental capacity is $1.12/hr/GPU. If the pool falls below the throughput floor for a 30‑minute window, Redwood issues a credit equal to 2x the incremental hourly charges for that 30‑minute outage (example numbers shown in amendment section 4, table). We'll produce a worked example with numbers for your budgeting sheet.
- 6‑month opt-out: we can offer a limited early-exit on the incremental 16 GPUs with a 60‑day notice after month 6, subject to a 15% termination fee on the remaining committed incremental hours. We'll put the exact mechanics in the amendment appendix.

Operational ramp plan (summary):
1) Signature day: effective amendment executed.
2) Week 1: provisioning + config drift checks (network & routing).
3) Week 2: staged canary (10% traffic to new GPUs), build verification harness.
4) Week 3: full ramp and 7-day validation window.

I'll also upload SOC2 AOC and current network diagram to your shared S3 link today.

— Dev
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, procure@horizonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — current committed pool + expansion questions

Liam — appreciate the rapid turnaround from your team and thanks for the SCQ file. Action items & next steps from Redwood: 
- We'll send a redline-ready amendment that includes: the incremental 16 GPU rate at $1.12/hr (with the prepay option at $0.98/hr), the pool-scoped throughput guarantee (1.1M tokens/hr combined), the sample credit calculation, and the 6‑month incremental opt-out mechanics.
- Marcus will follow up with a short two-line pricing summary for your budget sheet.
- Dev will upload SOC2 AOC + network diagram to the S3 share and I'll confirm when available.
- We'll prepare the mutual action plan with week-by-week milestones (signature → ramp → validation).

Proposed timing:
- Amendment & MOP to you by EOD Tuesday, 11 May.
- If that looks good, target signature by Friday, 14 May to begin provisioning the week of 17 May.

If that schedule works for Horizon, I'll include the DocuSign link in the amendment email when it's ready.

Thanks — Naomi
Head of Customer Success — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
